image_description: A close-up view of a crocodile swimming in water, with only the top of its head (eyes and snout ridge) and a portion of its armored back visible above the surface. The rest of the body is submerged. The water has ripples and reflections.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The full shape of the head and snout tip is obscured by the angle and water; only the eye ridge and part of the snout base are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and submerged/obscured; no teeth are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eyes are clearly visible protruding from the water on top of the head, consistent with dorsal positioning. Vertical slit pupils are discernible upon close inspection.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tip of the snout is either out of frame or obscured by water glare/angle; nostrils cannot be definitively located.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the back shows heavy armor/scutes, implying an elongated armored body typical of crocodilians.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct, rough, bony scutes are visible on the exposed back section, appearing in rows.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible scutes match the color description (dark/greyish-brown) and have a rough texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral surface (belly) is completely submerged and not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No limbs are visible above the water line.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is not visible in the frame.

artifact_observations.location: Water surface around the crocodile's head
artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight inconsistency in water ripple physics where the head breaks the surface; the displacement looks slightly 'painted' rather than physically displaced, but it is subtle.
Natural depth-of-field blur, but edges of some ripples in the mid-ground show slight smearing typical of AI generation.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species (Nile vs. other crocodilians) based on visible scute and head morphology.
To detect subtle blending errors or texture inconsistencies between the animal and the water.
To ensure the head is a single coherent object and not merging incorrectly with the water texture.

focus_areas: Scute texture and arrangement on the back
Water displacement realism around the head
Edge sharpness between subject and background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the eye reflection and pupil shape, as AI often fails to render vertical slit pupils correctly in low-light/water conditions. Verify if the scute pattern follows a logical biological progression or if it appears randomly generated/noisy. Check for 'melting' where the neck meets the water.

metadata.class_label: African crocodile, Nile crocodile, Crocodylus niloticus
